tldr: Treatment-initiation dates recorded in intervals preserve chronology between cells and conceal chronology within each cell. A positive independent audit identifies the doubled-hazard causal mean, but identification alone does not determine precision when audits are rare. The focal question is an explicit, uniform finite-sample characterization of absolute estimation risk and ninety-percent honest connected-interval length under an unknown bounded Borel initiation subdensity and a globally Hölder binary response. The representation by the outcome attached to the earlier of two natural initiation times connects recording error to audited pairs. The research claim is the joint information frontier and its necessary chart-review effort, rather than a new augmentation formula or an exact-time influence function.
gap: Ying, Zhao and Xu identifies a hazard-change mean and develops inference using exact dates. Cannings and Fan and Kim and coauthors provide general missing-data and semi-supervised pair methods. Their verified results do not evaluate the finite original-record experiment with common recording cells, an unknown within-cell timing law and shrinking independent audit probability.
fill: The project retains the fixed doubling policy, decomposes visible chronology from erased order, constructs an original-indicator correction, and seeks normalized legal mixture experiments with constant separated targets. It evaluates the full grid-dependent frontier, honest length and review-effort boundaries without imposing a nuisance rate, known subdensity or fixed realized audit count.
